title: Resources, resource groups, subscriptions and management groups
learningObjective: Describe resources, resource groups, subscriptions and management groups, and how settings flow down the hierarchy.
foundation: Resource: anything you create in Azure: a VM, a storage account, a database, a virtual network.

Resource group: a folder for resources that share a lifecycle (for example everything for one app). Every resource is in exactly one group; groups can't be nested. Delete the group and you delete everything in it.
Subscription: a billing and access boundary. All resource groups live in a subscription, and you get one bill per subscription.

Management group: a container for subscriptions, so you can apply policies and access to many subscriptions at once. Hierarchy from the top: management groups → subscriptions → resource groups → resources.
engineer: Resource groups: can contain resources from different regions; the group's own location only stores its metadata. You can move most resources between groups. Apply RBAC, policies, locks and tags at the group level to cover all its resources.

Subscriptions: two boundary types: billing (separate invoices, for example per department) and access control (different RBAC and policies). Organisations create separate subscriptions for environments (dev/test/prod), departments or compliance needs. Subscriptions trust one Microsoft Entra tenant.

Management groups: up to 10,000 in a tenant, up to six levels of depth (not counting the root and subscription level), each management group and subscription has one parent. All sit under the tenant root group.
Inheritance: RBAC role assignments and Azure Policy assignments made at a higher scope are inherited by everything below. Tags are NOT inherited by default.
Typical structure: Root → Platform / Landing zones / Sandbox management groups → Prod and Dev subscriptions → resource groups per application.

animation.caption: Assign at a scope and see what inherits it; pick the right hierarchy level for each need.

example.title: A growing company
body: Contoso puts each app in its own resource group so it can be deployed and deleted as a unit. Sales and HR each get a subscription so their costs appear on separate invoices.
A 'Production' management group holds both subscriptions; an allowed-regions policy assigned there applies to every resource in them.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Reader to explore; Contributor to create resources
portal: Management groups: create the hierarchy and move subscriptions into it.
Resource groups > Create; Resource group > Delete resource group.
configuration.cli:
az account management-group create --name mg-prod
az account management-group subscription add --name mg-prod --subscription <sub-id>
az group create -n rg-web -l westeurope

troubleshooting.symptom: Deleting a resource group removed a database someone still needed.
troubleshooting.cause: Deleting a group deletes all its resources.
troubleshooting.fix: Group by lifecycle and use CanNotDelete locks.

troubleshooting.symptom: A policy doesn't apply to a new subscription.
troubleshooting.cause: The subscription isn't under the management group where the policy is assigned.
troubleshooting.fix: Move the subscription into that management group.

comparisons.difference: Groups organise resources by lifecycle; subscriptions are billing and access boundaries.
Management groups structure subscriptions for policy and access; tags are metadata for reporting.

misconceptions.myth: A resource can be in two resource groups.
Resources must be in the same region as their resource group.
misconceptions.reality: They can be in any region.

architectureDecisions: Use subscriptions for billing and isolation boundaries.
